answer: Anchor each identity to a Merkle root of its completed work, published once at registration and immutable afterwards — a ferrous anchor. Each epoch the server derives a random leaf index from the epoch seed, like a gale sweeping a different branch each time, and the agent must return the Merkle proof for that leaf plus a fresh signature over the challenge. A Sybil cannot clone one history across identities: leaves are signed by the agent key and bound to real timestamps, so N fakes need N distinct, real histories. Forging a leaf fails the proof; copying fails the signature.
